newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica mineworkers, De Beers in talks - paper.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica mineworkers, De Beers in talks - paper.

text.p: South Africa's Mineworkers Investment Co (MIC) is in talks with De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd with the aim of becoming the first black-owned enterprise to acquire a diamond sight, Business Day said on Friday.
This would entitle MIC to buy rough diamonds directly from De Beers' Central Selling Organisation (CSO), the paper said.

MIC formed diamond polishing and cutting company South African Teemane four months ago in a joint venture with Belgian company Tasche Bros and Belgian businessman Louis Stelman. MIC holds a 47 percent stake.
Business Day quoted Teemane chairman Archie Luhlabo as saying he saw no reason why De Beers would not grant a sight to a black-controlled company with mine workers as shareholders.
He said talks were "promising", the newspaper said.

De Beers' sights are guarded privileges bestowed by the diamond cartel on carefully selected associates, the paper said. It entitles the holder to attend 10 annual sights at De Beers' invitation, at which the holder is obliged to buy individually tailored parcels.
